     2	# WP-001: Extract Persona Models Tab to Separate File
     3	
     4	## Plan Context
     5	
     6	Refactor the GUI server and frontend code introduced by the model-settings project to improve maintainability, fix a security info-disclosure pattern, add client-side validation UX, future-proof the orchestrator's persona file discovery, and establish test coverage for previously untested GUI components. No new features — purely technical debt, security hardening, and test coverage.
     7	
     8	## Description
     9	
    10	Extract all `pm*` state variables and functions from `config.js` into a new `config-persona-models.js` file, remove the vestigial pass-through parameters from the entire `pm*` forwarding chain (D5), and update the SPA shell HTML to load the new script.
    11	
    12	## Scope
    13	
    14	- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/config.js` — lines ~224–831 containing all `pm*` state, helpers, and functions
    15	- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/config-persona-models.js` — new file (extracted)
    16	- `mcp-server/gui/public/index.html` — new `<script>` tag for `config-persona-models.js`
    17	
    18	## Deliverables
    19	
    20	- New file `config-persona-models.js` containing all `pm*` module-level state variables (`pmModels`, `pmPersonas`, `pmAssignments`, `pmOriginal`, `pmIsBuilding`, `pmCollapsed`, `pmReplaceOpen`, `PM_SUITE_LABELS`, `PM_SUITE_ORDER`) and all `pm*` functions (`pmCloneAssignments`, `pmHasChanges`, `pmModelName`, `pmDirtyDot`, `pmBuildModelOptions`, `pmRefreshTab`, `pmBuildTabHtml`, `pmWireEvents`, `pmDoSave`, `pmDoRebuild`)
    21	- Vestigial pass-through parameters removed from the `pm*` forwarding chain:
    22	  - `pmWireEvents(config, models, personas, assignments)` → `pmWireEvents()`
    23	  - `pmRefreshTab(config, models, personas, assignments)` → `pmRefreshTab()`
    24	  - `pmDoRebuild(config, models, personas, assignments)` → `pmDoRebuild()`
    25	  - `pmDoSave(config, models, personas, assignments)` → `pmDoSave()`
    26	- All call sites updated: `renderConfigTabContent()` in `config.js` (calls `pmWireEvents`), event-handler lambdas inside `pmWireEvents` (call `pmRefreshTab`, `pmDoRebuild`, `pmDoSave`), and the async re-fetch path inside `pmDoRebuild` (calls `pmRefreshTab`)
    27	- Updated `index.html` with `<script src="/views/config-persona-models.js?v=1"></script>` tag before the `config.js` tag
    28	- `config.js` reduced by ~608 lines (lines 224–831 moved out)
    29	
    30	## Dependencies
    31	
    32	- None
    33	
    34	## Acceptance Criteria
    35	
    36	1. config-persona-models.js exists and contains all pm* state variables and functions — no pm* definitions remain in config.js
    37	2. The Persona Models tab renders identically to the pre-extraction version (same HTML output, same event handling behavior)
    38	3. The vestigial pass-through parameters are removed from all four functions: pmWireEvents, pmRefreshTab, pmDoRebuild, and pmDoSave — all have zero-argument signatures
    39	4. All call sites updated accordingly: renderConfigTabContent passes no arguments to pmWireEvents, event-handler lambdas inside pmWireEvents pass no arguments to pmRefreshTab/pmDoRebuild/pmDoSave, and the async re-fetch path inside pmDoRebuild passes no arguments to pmRefreshTab
    40	5. The <script> tag for config-persona-models.js is present in index.html and loads before config.js
    41	6. Cross-tab interactions work correctly: configDirty.personaModels updates from pm* functions are visible to the coordinator's beforeTabSwitch() guard
    42	
    43	## Active Pipeline Stages
    44	
    45	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    46	
    47	## Estimated Complexity
    48	
    49	Medium
    50	
    51	## Rationale
    52	
    53	Per-tab file splitting mirrors the logical separation already enforced by the `pm*` prefix convention. The dead parameter cleanup (D5) is bundled here because these parameters are artifacts of the pre-extraction forwarding chain — removing them during extraction is the natural time to do so.
    54	
    55	## Rejected Approaches
    56	
    57	- *Keep monolithic config.js:* At 1395 lines with 3 tabs, the file crossed the complexity threshold during the model-settings project and is difficult to navigate.
    58	- *One file per function group:* Too granular for a vanilla-JS SPA without a module system — per-tab is the natural boundary.
    59	- *Defer D5 dead parameter cleanup to a separate WP:* The parameters are vestigial forwarding artifacts — removing them during extraction avoids carrying dead code into the new file and updating call sites twice.
    60	
    61	## Notes
    62	
    63	The new file must load BEFORE `config.js` in the SPA shell because `config.js` calls `pmWireEvents()` from `renderConfigTabContent()`. The `pm*` functions reference `configDirty` (defined in `config.js`) via the shared global scope. The `renderConfigTabContent()` call site in `config.js` (line 135) currently passes `(config, models, personas, assignments)` to `pmWireEvents` — this call must be updated to pass no arguments. Independent of WP-004 — `pm*` and `mr*` functions have no cross-references.
    64	
    65	## Code Observations
    66	
    67	Inspected `config.js` (1395 lines). Persona Models state and functions span lines 224–831 (608 lines). The `pmWireEvents` function is called at line 135 with `(config, models, personas, assignments)` — all four parameters are passed through from `renderConfigTabContent()` which receives them from `renderConfigPage()`. The `pm*` functions reference `configDirty.personaModels` (global), `API.updateAssignments` / `API.rebuildPersonas` / `API.getAssignments` / `API.getPersonas` / `API.getModels` (global), and DOM utilities. The forwarding chain: `renderConfigTabContent → pmWireEvents → event lambdas → pmRefreshTab/pmDoSave/pmDoRebuild`. All four functions in the chain receive the same `(config, models, personas, assignments)` tuple but only reference module-level `pm*` state internally — the parameters are vestigial.

1	
     2	# WP-005: Server Route Dispatch Refactor
     3	
     4	## Plan Context
     5	
     6	Refactor the GUI server and frontend code introduced by the model-settings project to improve maintainability, fix a security info-disclosure pattern, add client-side validation UX, future-proof the orchestrator's persona file discovery, and establish test coverage for previously untested GUI components. No new features — purely technical debt, security hardening, and test coverage.
     7	
     8	## Description
     9	
    10	Define a typed `BodyRoute` interface and declarative route table, implement a `dispatchBodyRoute()` dispatcher function, and replace all ~18 inline try/catch body-parsing blocks in `handleRequest()` with a single dispatcher call — reducing `handleRequest()` from ~500+ lines to ~70–80 lines.
    11	
    12	## Scope
    13	
    14	- `mcp-server/gui/server.ts` — the 1994-line server file containing `handleRequest()` with ~18 duplicated inline route blocks (lines ~1509–1908)
    15	- `mcp-server/gui/server.ts` — new `BodyRoute` type definition and `dispatchBodyRoute()` function (added to the same file or a dedicated `route-types.ts`)
    16	
    17	## Deliverables
    18	
    19	- `BodyRoute` typed interface with `method`, `path` (string or RegExp with named capture groups), `handler`, optional `statusCode`, and optional `noBody` fields
    20	- `BodyRoute[]` route table containing all ~18 migrated body-parsing routes, with closure variables (`ledgerRoot`, `configPath`, `orchestratorLogsDir`, `bootVersions`) captured via arrow functions
    21	- `dispatchBodyRoute()` function that iterates the route table, matches requests, conditionally parses the body, calls the handler, and handles the full error chain (`PayloadTooLargeError` → `ApiError` → generic error)
    22	- Refactored `handleRequest()` reduced to ~70–80 lines: OPTIONS preflight → static serving → body dispatch → `matchRoute()` fallback → 404
    23	- All non-standard response patterns preserved: `statusCode: 204` (empty response, skip `sendJson()`), `noBody: true` (skip `readJsonBody()`), `ApiError` throws for conditional failures (e.g. rebuild), custom status codes (201 for POST /api/repos)
    24	- Deprecated non-namespaced routes preserved in the route table
    25	
    26	## Dependencies
    27	
    28	- None
    29	
    30	## Acceptance Criteria
    31	
    32	1. handleRequest() in server.ts is reduced to ≤80 lines (from ~500+ lines of inline body-route blocks), with all routes delegated to a declarative route table + dispatcher function
    33	2. All ~18 body-parsing routes produce identical HTTP responses (status codes, error shapes, headers) as before refactoring — verified by the full existing GUI test suite passing without assertion changes
    34	3. The BodyRoute interface is defined with typed fields: method, path (string | RegExp), handler, optional statusCode, optional noBody
    35	4. All path: RegExp entries in the route table use named capture groups (?<name>…) — no positional group indexing
    36	5. The dispatcher correctly handles noBody: true routes (skips readJsonBody()), statusCode: 204 routes (writes empty response, skips sendJson()), and ApiError throws (delegates to apiErrorToStatus())
    37	6. Deprecated non-namespaced routes (PATCH /api/projects/:slug, POST /api/projects/:slug/reset, etc.) are preserved in the route table
    38	
    39	## Active Pipeline Stages
    40	
    41	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    42	
    43	## Estimated Complexity
    44	
    45	High
    46	
    47	## Rationale
    48	
    49	The synthesis recommended bundling the server.ts refactor into a maintainability work package. `handleRequest()` has 18 identical try/catch blocks producing ~270 lines of duplicated boilerplate. A declarative route table is minimal, zero-dependency, and scales better than the current inline approach.
    50	
    51	## Rejected Approaches
    52	
    53	- *Express/Koa framework:* Adds an external dependency to a zero-dependency HTTP server — overengineered for a flat route list.
    54	- *Class-based Router:* Over-engineered for a flat route list with no middleware requirements.
    55	- *Keep inline blocks:* Doesn't scale — already at 18 blocks and growing with each new route.
    56	
    57	## Notes
    58	
    59	This is the highest-complexity WP and cannot be split further because all routes must migrate atomically — a half-migrated `handleRequest()` with some routes inline and some dispatched would be harder to maintain than the current state. The existing GUI test suite (3,523+ tests) serves as the regression safety net. Routes requiring closure variables must use arrow functions or a factory function to capture scope.
    60	
    61	## Code Observations
    62	
    63	Inspected `server.ts` (1994 lines). `handleRequest()` starts at line 1481 and runs through line 1929 (~448 lines). Contains 13 `readJsonBody()` calls (some routes like `GET /api/config`, `GET /api/server-info` don't parse bodies but are still inline). The `matchRoute()` fallback (body-free GET/DELETE routes) is at line 1912 and is NOT being refactored — it stays as-is. All inline blocks follow the identical pattern: method+path check → `readJsonBody()` → handler call → `sendJson()` → catch chain. Non-standard cases: POST `/api/repos` returns 201, orchestrator dismiss/delete/kill routes return 204, personas/rebuild has a conditional `ApiError` throw. Deprecated non-namespaced routes exist for `PATCH /api/projects/:slug` and `POST /api/projects/:slug/reset`.
